minutes.headline: Capital Planning Committee began open discussion of FY25 capital requests, with no votes on priorities; members will rank items individually.
minutes.summary: The committee held its first free-form prioritization discussion after hearing all department presentations. Debate covered school items (Turkey Hill windows and the MSBA programs, window safety film), town building items (Marshall Pond weed treatment, Wallace Park courts, senior center parking design, North Cemetery wall) and a DPW front-end loader. The chair explained that members will rank every item one to N by email before the Dec. 18 meeting; the only vote was to adjourn.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment at the start; none is recorded in the captions.
A person asked whether the window film ranking is split across three projects on the spreadsheet; it was agreed the project numbering needs fixing.
Chair asked again for public comment and saw none.

budget_items.topic: School safety (window film) request by building
budget_items.what_was_said: A member noted the per-building breakdown totals differently than the original district-wide request and asked about an unlabeled amount; the school representative did not know the reason and will get an answer.
The project cost was noted as changed from the original figure to a different amount; members debated whether chemical treatment is a recurring cost.
The project was split into design and construction with a new project number for design.
Members noted the stair item is relatively small dollars compared with other projects.
Members asked for the history of earlier resurfacing and repair spending and what the installer expected for lifespan.
A member said design should be allowed to assess available space, including moving Kids Kingdom.
Members questioned a roof cost as very high compared with professional opinions.
A member objected to buying a new loader while keeping the old one, expecting another purchase in a few years.
Members questioned the cost of the wall and arborvitae replacement and whether a barrier is needed at all.
A member suggested some drainage work may be fundable through grants or earmarks.

decisions.decision: A member will email the facility superintendent for the Wallace Park resurfacing history and share it with the committee.

The chair and town manager will circulate a spreadsheet of all items; members rank every item one to N with no blanks or duplicates, keeping spreadsheet order, and email only to the chair by about Dec. 16.
Next meetings set for Monday December 18 and Thursday December 21 at 6 pm in the same room.
Window film project numbering to be fixed so it is not ranked as three separate projects.
Prior minutes to be reviewed and approved pro forma at a later meeting.

what_happened.line: The Capital Planning Committee held its first open discussion of FY25 capital requests and took no votes on priorities; the only vote was to adjourn.
Members will each rank every item one to N on a shared spreadsheet and email the ranking only to the chair by about Dec. 16.
Members debated school window safety film, Marshall Pond weed treatment, Wallace Park courts, senior center parking design, the North Cemetery wall and a DPW front-end loader.
A member objected to buying a new DPW loader with plow while keeping the old one, and the debate ended without resolution.
The window film request is to be renumbered so it is not ranked as three separate projects, after a question during public comment.

why_it_matters: These individual rankings will shape which FY25 capital requests, such as school windows, a loader, and park and cemetery work, go forward to a town vote.
Rankings are sent privately by email to the chair, so the committee's priorities will not be visible until a later public meeting.
watch_next: Committee meetings on Monday Dec. 18 and Thursday Dec. 21 at 6 pm, after members' rankings are due about Dec. 16.
The answers promised on the window film totals and the Wallace Park resurfacing history.
